issues.claim: `list[0]` ... это вызов индексатора ... Для типа значения такой метод возвращает копию элемента - значение, а не переменную (cited to the List<T>.Item page)
issues.problem: The sandbox confirms CS1612, and the claim is correct from the language rules. But the fetched List<T>.Item excerpt says nothing about copy or value semantics. It only says the indexer gets or sets the element and that its get is O(1). The struct page excerpt covers readonly structs, immutability and the compiler copying for readonly members, not the 'array element is a variable, indexer result is a value' rule. The generator notes admit this. The CollectionsMarshal.AsSpan claim (available since .NET 5, Span indexer returns ref T, do not resize the list while the span is in use) has no cited source at all.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a link to the Microsoft Learn page for Compiler Error CS1612 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/misc/cs1612), with linkTitles in both locales. Add a link to the CollectionsMarshal.AsSpan<T>(List<T>) docs for the span bullet, or remove the '.NET 5' and resize-warning details. Keep the Item page only for the claim that the indexer is the get accessor of Item.

issues.claim: Элемент массива - это переменная, поэтому `array[0].X = 5` меняет саму структуру внутри массива. Но до запуска дело всё равно не доходит
issues.problem: Option d is '1 1', which says neither write took effect. The explanation only discusses the array line, so it does not say why the list write is not silently lost either, and it leans on option c's explanation for that.
issues.suggestedFix: Add one sentence: both writes cannot be lost, because the array write succeeds and the list write is rejected at compile time, so no output at all is printed.

issues.claim: поэтому выбор строки 9 или обеих строк тоже принимается / so selecting line 9 or both lines is also accepted
issues.problem: The reference answer exposes grading mechanics (which line selections are accepted) instead of just stating the answer. bugLineSets [[10],[9],[9,10]] is defensible. Line 10 `    entry.Count++;` mutates only the copy and nothing is written back. Line 9 `    Stats entry = stats[word];` is where the copy is made.
issues.suggestedFix: Rewrite as: 'The defect is on lines 9-10: `Stats entry = stats[word];` makes a copy, and `entry.Count++` changes only that copy, which is never written back.'

issues.problem: The loop as written does ContainsKey, then the indexer get, then the write-back set (plus the first-time `new Stats()` insert), so it is more than two lookups.
issues.suggestedFix: Say 'an extra lookup per word' or 'several key lookups per word' instead of 'two'.
